answer: Quadratic stake weighting blocks Sybils: an agent's vote equals the square of the collateral it locks, not how many identities it holds. One operator can harbor a hundred fake wallets, but splitting a stake shrinks their summed weight, so each extra name dilutes power. Each consensus pulse burns a fee and slashes equivocators, so the attacker pays locked capital up front and loses it if caught. Even a plume of new identities cannot sway a vote, since ten small stakes weigh a hundredth of one equal-sized stake. The cost to attack is real capital, not cheap accounts.
